```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# Browser cache key, derived from the database's own bytes.
#
# It used to be the release tag:
#     "multised-refined@v0.2.0"
# That was wrong. The database is re-uploaded onto the EXISTING release rather
# than tagged afresh, so the tag does not move when the file changes, and every
# returning visitor went on serving the stale copy out of browser cache. That
# surfaces as "no such column" the moment a rebuild adds one, which the August
# 2026 rebuild did: extraction_class, accredited, frac_basis, pressure_class and
# the fish-farm columns are all new. Hashing the file is exact by construction:
# same bytes, same key; new bytes, new key.
#
# It also stays correct under DB_RELEASE, which pins an older release when
# reproducing a build: the hash follows whichever file the pre-render step
# actually fetched, where a tag-derived key would have to be remembered.
ojs_define(
  dbCacheKey = paste0(
    "multised-refined@",
    substr(unname(tools::md5sum("multised_refined.sqlite")), 1, 12)
  )
)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
db = {
  const StratumSQLite = await window._stratumSQLite;
  return StratumSQLite.open(window._dbRefined, {
    sqlJsPath: window._sqljsBase,
    cacheKey:  dbCacheKey,
  });
}
```
